objective: Assess whether ForgeWorld's own repo can demonstrate offline phone->laptop continuity

source_context.raw_text: Repo has substrate/ built last session but no phone-native sensor mission object yet | context: Continuity Substrate Ascension V1 directive, module 01

evidence.description: Promoted from sensor mission PSM-20260703T215640Z-1840: This directive text + prior substrate/README.md

artifacts_created.description: Ascension modules 01-10: sensor-capture.sh, promote-sensor-mission.sh, build-evidence-package.sh, update-capability-genome.sh, update-relationship-graph.sh, export-desktop-packet.sh, governance-check.sh, instrumentation.sh, extended substrate-status.sh

validation_results.result: sensor-capture -> promote -> evidence package -> capability genome -> relationship graph -> desktop export manifest all ran successfully against this mission's own data; duplicate detection and deterministic export both verified

commercial_opportunities.problem_solved: Phone captures were previously ad hoc text; there was no schema-validated, governed, offline-first sensor object feeding the same continuity substrate as the laptop
commercial_opportunities.notes: This ascension layer is itself the productized capability: phone-native mission capture with governance, evidence packaging, and deterministic sync, sellable as a feature of the ForgeWorld substrate product

lessons_learned: A read-only export step must never mutate the very files it hashes - discovered this by testing determinism twice in a row and catching a self-referential hash drift bug before it shipped
Bash array expansion under 'set -u' silently produces a stray empty-string element ([''] instead of []) unless filtered - caught by testing capability genome merges twice, not by reading the code
next_recommended_action: Wire promote-sensor-mission.sh + build-evidence-package.sh + update-capability-genome.sh into a single guided phone-to-laptop sync command so an operator doesn't have to run 4 scripts by hand
